address: Kloveniersburgwal 72 (former Binnengasthuis, now University of Amsterdam), Amsterdam: Nieuwe Hoogstraat row-house fronts, the 1900s GASTHUIS APOTHEEK brick range, a 1930s curved brick wing and a 1950s beige block
notes: Kloveniersburgwal 72 (BAG, built 1757 core) is the former Binnengasthuis block (now University of Amsterdam) between Nieuwe Hoogstraat, Kloveniersburgwal and Oudezijds Achterburgwal; 468 3DBAG wall surfaces round several courts. Six photographed street runs are drawn (w01-16, w06-192, w04-121, w02-122, w05-121, w03-300); courts, the long south front (panel 55, no photograph) and every other wall stay blank (otherWalls).

walls[0] = the north run on Nieuwe Hoogstraat (panel 10, 9.4 m surfaces only): three storeys of row-house fronts with white-framed windows over shopfronts, cornice. The 12 m gable surfaces and the 7.7 m surface are left blank. 6 bays of ~4 m stand for the ~20 narrower row-house axes (22 bays cost 16k tris).

walls[1] = panel 56 (w06-192): the 1900s brick range with grey stone ground storey, iron-barred windows and the arched GASTHUIS APOTHEEK portal. Drawn as 4 storeys x 3 bays, a portal entrance in bay 2 and GASTHUIS APOTHEEK fascia lettering. Simplified: the carved cartouche, scrolls and the sculpture group on the right pier, the iron window grilles.

walls[2] = panel 60 (w04-121): the 1930s brick wing with the white curved window band, drawn as 4 storeys of wide windows with white string courses; the curved bay and the wrap-round balcony band are straight. walls[3] = panel 286 (w02-122): the 1950s beige block, 4 storeys x 7 bays of plain windows. walls[4] = four 14.5 m surfaces of the canal gable row (w05-121), 4 storeys x 4 bays; the gables are the 3DBAG roof. walls[5] = panel 12 (w03-300): the grey-blue brick wing with a curved front, 4 storeys x 5 bays; the curve is straight.
Not drawn: the long south front (panel 55) and the inner court walls (no panorama within 35 m); the green copper roof of the curved wing.
